clue.text: Bowled, chance of a draw wasted

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
a lottery draw gives a chance to win; lotto is that game

explanation.surface: A cricket match ends with the batsman bowled and any hope of a draw thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' suggests a drawn cricket match, but here it is a prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for extremely drunk.

clue.text: See 19
Woody Allen movie, black melodrama, hero ultimately sent up

indicators.note: in a down entry sent up means read from bottom to top
ultimately takes the final letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A Woody Allen film, a dark melodrama, ends with the hero mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woody' plus 'Allen' look like one name; 'Woody' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken means made of oak, so it is wooden, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: xposed?

parts.note: the word exposed printed with its first letter cut off shows a word missing its top

explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the first letter is the top; dropping E from exposed makes it lack its top, and to lack a top is to be exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a top garment means bare-chested, so exposed in a literal clothing sense.

clue.text: Cutter in dance is no longer tacking?

parts.note: a jig is a lively folk dance

indicators.note: a tacking boat changes direction, so these letters turn round and run the other way

parts.note: is put into the past tense, as it is no longer so, gives was

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether a dancer has stopped sewing with loose stitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tacking' looks like sewing or sailing, but signals WAS reversed to SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a saw for cutting curved shapes, so it is a cutting tool.

clue.text: In the same book, I remain magnificent, initially

parts.note: to bide is to remain or wait

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word magnificent

explanation.surface: A boastful character says they stay superb throughout one volume.
explanation.walkthrough: IBIDEM is the Latin used in footnotes, often shortened to ibid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin term is used in references to cite the same source as the previous note.

clue.text: Lumps in it perhaps, take up American dress on creature of the night

indicators.note: in a down light on places one piece above the next
in a down entry, taking up a piece makes it read from the bottom

parts.note: US is short for United States, American
garb is clothing or dress
an owl is a nocturnal bird

explanation.surface: An owl in American clothes is dressed for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lumps' are sugar lumps, and the question mark marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar bowl holds sugar, which may come as lumps or cubes.

clue.text: How novel twice has inspired second reference book

indicators.note: has inspired means has breathed in, holding the letter inside
twice means the rearranged piece appears two times
novel means new, so the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A novel which twice inspires a second reference work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but signals rearranging HOW to WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Who's Who is an annual directory of notable people, an example of a reference work.

clue.text: Bones to cover still, penning a fine book

indicators.note: to cover means to go around the outside of the rest

parts.note: bones is old slang for dice, which were once made of bone

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: still in the sense of smooth or level means even
fine as in slender means thin

explanation.surface: Skeleton remains covered with a fine book.
explanation.walkthrough: Death in Venice is Thomas Mann's novella.
explanation.definitionFit: Death in Venice is a novella by Thomas Mann, an example of a literary work.

clue.text: See 21
Someone spying first of pins grasped by marker of territory?

indicators.note: grasped by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: a tomcat urinating, a peeing tom, marks out its territory by scent

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the word pins

explanation.surface: A spy is identified by the pins held by someone who stakes out ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey cat image: a peeing tom marks territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyeur who secretly watches others is called a Peeping Tom, after the Lady Godiva legend.

clue.text: Spring, when one has cup upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone leaps up the moment a cup gets knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring on prey is to leap at it suddenly, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: See 23
SIX (not 9) sides in vessel

indicators.note: IX is the Roman numeral nine, and not says it is taken away from the word six

parts.note: sides in a match are teams
in means fashionable, as does hip

explanation.surface: A boat is said to have six sides minus something.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is Roman IX, so SIX less IX leaves S.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a vessel powered by steam engines, an example of a ship.

clue.text: Animal appendage getting a bash, suffering cuts

parts.note: an arm is a limb, an appendage

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bash is a party, as is a do
suffering means being ill

explanation.surface: A limb takes a blow and gets cut up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' suggests a blow but means a party, DO.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: How one's coffee may be ordered in African country

definitions.text: How one's coffee may be ordered
definitions.meaning: a takeaway coffee is ordered to take out, in two words
a small West African state between Ghana and Benin

explanation.surface: A café order meets a geography question.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee ordered 'to go' is takeaway, and Togo is a West African nation.

clue.text: For all to see in May for example, a wild animal

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: Theresa May was a Prime Minister, PM
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: In May a wild animal is out in the open for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month, but is Theresa May, a British Prime Minister; 'in' puts U inside PM.
explanation.definitionFit: A puma is a large wild cat of the Americas, also called a cougar.

clue.text: Start low, catching French horn up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read bottom to top
catching means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: deep, as of a voice, means low
cor is the French word for horn

explanation.surface: A French horn player starts low and climbs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' is an instrument in the surface, but is French for horn, COR.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed is to begin or go ahead with something, a synonym for start.

clue.text: Lover's pet snakes failed to stir

indicators.note: snakes as a verb means winds about, so the letters twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A beloved pet's snakes failed to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snakes' looks like the plural noun, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who overslept stayed asleep past the time and did not wake or move.

clue.text: Cleric guarding a nuclear structure

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding and protecting, holding a inside

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A priest guards a nuclear plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the structure in which nuclear fission is controlled.

clue.text: Go to town, or go to sea?

definitions.meaning: to go to town means to spend lavishly or celebrate extravagantly
literally, launching a boat from shore takes it to sea

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to spend freely, and literally describes launching a vessel.

clue.text: Stocked by libraries, the reference book

indicators.note: stocked by means kept inside, so letters are held within these words

explanation.surface: Libraries carry the reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reference book' reads as one phrase, but only 'book' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Skilful, I start crossing on football ground

parts.note: skilful means good, as in good at something

indicators.note: the word on lies across the middle of the other piece, which straddles it

parts.note: to spark something off is to start it

explanation.surface: A talented player gets going by crossing on to the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: GOODISON PARK is Everton FC's stadium in Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the home stadium of Everton Football Club, an example of a football venue.

clue.text: Help player, having missed header

indicators.note: missing the header means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a bassist is a musician who plays bass

explanation.surface: A footballer helps out after missing a header.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header' suggests football, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help; both are verbs (and nouns) for giving aid.

clue.text: Man alive seen to empty trash out before a murder

indicators.note: before puts this piece ahead of the next
out means disordered, so these letters are rearranged
empty removes the inside, leaving only the outer letters of trash

parts.note: a murder is the collective noun for a flock of crows

explanation.surface: A man is seen emptying rubbish before a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SEENTO plus TH (empty 'trash') into STONE THE; 'a murder' is crows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British exclamations of surprise or amazement.

clue.text: Having suffered main loss in difficult battle, Chelsea take on dangerous responsibility

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are troubled and in disorder
the main is a poetic word for the open sea, and losing it removes those letters from Chelsea

explanation.surface: Chelsea football club, losing a hard battle, take on a risky task.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea less SEA gives CHEL; 'difficult' rearranges BATTLE CHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a fable of mice choosing one to put a bell on the cat, a perilous mission.

clue.text: Curse at my gags

indicators.note: gags means stops the mouth, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: my as an exclamation of surprise equals oh

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a comedian's jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gags' looks like a comedian's jokes, but here it means muffles, the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a swear word, a profane exclamation.

clue.text: Nothing coming in when delivery happened, track item without a name?

indicators.note: coming in puts the piece inside the other

parts.note: date of birth, abbreviated DOB, is when a baby was delivered
nothing is zero, the letter O
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A railway delivery note lists an unnamed item and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: DOOBRY is British slang for a thingummy, something whose name escapes you.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a placeholder word for a thing whose name one cannot recall, like whatsit.

clue.text: Comic's ending in second place — that's easy

indicators.note: the final letter is moved to become the second letter

parts.note: The Beezer was a British children's comic

explanation.surface: A comedian's finish comes second, which is easy going.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beezer was a British children's comic (1956-1993); its last letter shifts to second.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is something very easy, an informal idiom: it was a breeze.
